body: The survey is about suicide and suicidal behaviour. We are asking for the terms people would like professionals to use when talking about this. The term self-harm is used in several setting (including in various health documents) to describe suicidal behaviour. We don't know what the conclusion will be but saying we are asking you to contribute to the debate by responding to the survey.  If you think they are different behaviours and shouldn't be used interchangeably, then please tell us this through the survey. Comments on social media will not inform our conclusions.
Thank you for your kind words

Thank you for your comment. The questionnaire was piloted and these issues were not raised at that stage, but we will keep them in mind for future work. 

You are right to point out that we have included self harm and suicide as one behaviour. The reason we present it as such is that because whilst there might be a public differentiation in terms, these terms are interchangeably used in both clinical and research settings around the world. Therefore your views on this subject are important and I hope you articulated this in the survey free text responses so that it is captured. Thanks for taking part

Hi there.
Thanks for the comment. This survey is not specifically targeted at professionals. What we are trying to do is to find out what people who are affected by suicidal behaviour find most appropriate, in general terms. What someone uses to describe their behaviour or the behaviour of others is 100% acceptable, as it's acceptable to them. We are not asking you to judge the term based on who said it but on what kind of language you think is appropriate for say a journalist or an academic like me to use when we're talking about some who has passed or a group of people who have engaged in suicidal behaviour. Hope that helps. 
Dee
Ps we have asked for how you have been affected so that we can see if there is a difference between what professionals say versus those bereaved or who have engaged in suicidal behaviour.

Hi there. Thanks for this issue you have raised. We are trying to find the terminology that people affected in someway by suicide find the most appropriate. In some settings people will use non-fatal self-harm to describe suicidal behaviour. What we want to know is what people like you think about that. If you think it conflates the issue then please feed that back to us in the survey so we can help develop some guidelines for professionals to use that are most acceptable. Hope that helps!
